text:
Philadelphia took a 2-1 lead into the third period on the strength of Joseph Woll, who faced 40 shots and saved 1.79 goals more than the chances deserved. Carolina's edge in play was far bigger than the final margin: 4.79 expected goals to 2.83, 79 shot attempts to 43, and a 78 percent share of simulated replays won. The second period was the clearest example. CAR out-chanced PHI 2.78 to 0.53, and William Carrier's 66 percent look was stopped by Woll, yet Matvei Michkov's wrist shot at 7:20 was the only goal of the period.

Sebastian Aho opened the scoring 10 seconds in on a snap shot worth just a 5 percent chance, the least likely goal of the night. Owen Tippett answered at 8:03 of the first, and Michkov's 26 percent chance gave PHI the lead in the second. Carolina leaned on its power play to turn pressure into goals. Aho tied it at 4:59 of the third with a man advantage, finishing a night of two goals and an assist while his line held a 2.28 to 0.57 expected goals edge.

The winner came in overtime, again on the power play. Shayne Gostisbehere's slap shot at 2:51 made it CAR 3, PHI 2, with assists to Jackson Blake and Aho. Carolina went 2 for 4 on the power play to Philadelphia's 0 for 4, though the expected goals on those chances were nearly even, so the special teams gap owed something to finishing. Pyotr Kochetkov faced only 18 shots and stopped 16 in the win.
